Group.title: Group
Group.description: Represents a group or flat within the NourishTrack application, enabling shared meal and expense tracking.

id.description: Unique identifier for the group entity.

groupName.description: The name of the group or flat.

invitationCode.description: Unique code used for users to join the group.

adminId.description: Reference to User who is the administrator of the group. (Relationship: User 1:N Group)

memberIds.description: References to Users who are members of the group. (Relationship: Group 1:N User)

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user within the NourishTrack application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

groupId.description: Reference to Group that the user belongs to.  If null, the user does not belong to a group. (Relationship: Group 1:N User)

isAdmin.description: Indicates whether the user is an administrator of a group.

Member.title: Member
Member.description: Represents a member within a group, containing their email and role.

role.description: The role of the member within the group (e.g., 'admin', 'member').

joinedAt.description: The timestamp when the member joined the group.

MealLog.title: MealLog
MealLog.description: Represents a meal log entry for a user, including details about the meal and its associated date.

id.description: Unique identifier for the meal log entry.

groupId.description: Reference to Group that the meal log belongs to. (Relationship: Group 1:N MealLog)

userId.description: Reference to User who created the meal log. (Relationship: User 1:N MealLog)

mealType.description: The type of meal (e.g., breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack).

date.description: The date when the meal was consumed.

Expense.title: Expense
Expense.description: Represents an expense incurred by a user, including details about the amount, date, category, and an optional receipt photo.

id.description: Unique identifier for the expense entry.

groupId.description: Reference to Group that the expense belongs to. (Relationship: Group 1:N Expense)

userId.description: Reference to User who incurred the expense. (Relationship: User 1:N Expense)

date.description: The date when the expense was incurred.

PurchasedItem.title: PurchasedItem
PurchasedItem.description: Represents a purchased item, including details about the quantity, unit, and cost.

id.description: Unique identifier for the purchased item.

groupId.description: Reference to Group that the purchased item belongs to. (Relationship: Group 1:N PurchasedItem)

userId.description: Reference to User who purchased the item. (Relationship: User 1:N PurchasedItem)

name.description: The name of the purchased item.

quantity.description: The quantity of the purchased item.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the purchased item.

cost.description: The cost of the purchased item.

date.description: The date the item was purchased.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed for a secure, multi-tenant application where users are organized into groups. Authorization is paramount, and the structure is built to support Query-based Access Protocols (QAPs) by denormalizing key information.

Key Authorization & Data Modeling Decisions:

1.  **/groups/{groupId}**: This is the central document for each group. It contains an `adminId` and a `memberIds` array. This document is the source of truth for who belongs to a group and who can manage it. Security rules will heavily reference this document to check for membership (`request.auth.uid in resource.data.memberIds`).

2.  **/groups/{groupId}/members/{memberId}**: This subcollection was added to securely list group members. Instead of querying the top-level `/users` collection (which would require overly broad read permissions), the application can query this subcollection. Security rules can easily protect this path by checking if the requesting user is a member of the parent group (e.g., `get(/databases/(default)/documents/groups/$(groupId)).data.memberIds.hasAny([request.auth.uid])`). This prevents users from listing members of groups they don't belong to and is a textbook example of secure data modeling for list operations.

3.  **/users/{userId}**: This collection stores user-specific, non-group-related data. The `groupId` field here is for UI convenience (e.g., quickly finding a user's group) and should **not** be the basis for security rules, as a user could tamper with their own document. Authorization should always be based on the `/groups/{groupId}` document.

4.  **Group Subcollections (`meals`, `expenses`, `purchasedItems`)**: All group-specific content is stored in subcollections under the relevant group document. This provides natural data scoping. Security rules for these paths will always verify that the user is part of the parent `groupId` before allowing any read or write operation, ensuring data is only accessible to group members.

5.  **Authorization Independence**: By placing `groupId` and `userId` directly within documents in the `meals`, `expenses`, and `purchasedItems` subcollections, we achieve authorization independence. Security rules can validate access without needing to perform extra `get()` calls to other documents, which is more performant and secure. For example, a rule for `meals` can check `resource.data.groupId == groupId` and that the user is a member of that group.
